reviews.title: Longtime user frustrated by iOS version
reviews.text:
I’ve used Google Tasks for 10+ years, multiple times a day, with 30–40 lists containing everything from daily tasks to personal notes, memories, work information, and even detailed lists of what’s in my storage bins. It’s become an important personal reference system.

After switching from Android to iPhone about a year ago, I’ve been extremely frustrated by how limited the iOS version is compared with Android. And now, in the latest update, a particularly useful feature appears to have been removed: the drop-down menu in the upper-left corner that let you quickly see and select from all your lists.

With dozens of lists, having to scroll horizontally through them is significantly slower and more cumbersome. I genuinely don’t understand why such a basic and useful feature would be removed.

Please bring it back—and please give the iOS version the same functionality as Android. Longtime users like me depend on this app, and it’s frustrating to see it become less useful over time. I’m now being forced to look for something different. Ugg!

reviews.title: Please update your app!
reviews.text:
1) The Widget is borderline useless especially the square one. The rectangle one isn’t as bad. 

2) The UI is bad, old looking, lacks modern appeal. 

3) No badge support so you don’t know what’s due unless you use the widget or open the app. It goes in the Notification Center and that’s it. 

4) No logic for entry; “Do the laundry at 6 PM on Monday” will literally just write that out instead of adding those times. 

5) No voice integration with Siri like Microsoft ToDo and other Reminder/Tasks apps. 

6) No meaningful updates. It’s in maintenance mode. Look at the history and you’ll see nothing substantial for years!

Despite this being part of the Google ecosystem just like Google’s other mishap (Keep) it is not a useful tool. You can add some tasks and that’s it. It has Calendar integration (not required tbh). But it doesn’t have any share functionality and I’m not talking about corporate integration but rather if you want to have a shared grocery list with your spouse then you’re screwed. 
Todoist is better but the paid plan is too expensive for a family organizer. 
So I guess I’m back to MS To-Do.

reviews.title: Pros: Free, works with Google Calendar. Cons: Everything else
reviews.text:
If you use Google calendar, and want a free, bare-bones To-Do List app that will show up on said calendar - this is that, and almost only that.

If you need a well-designed task app, that does anything else other than that: flee. 

Leaving aside that Google is the Internet equivalent of an all-seeing, all-knowing, amoral God, moonlighting as a giant billboard: 

• No search function (this is Google we’re talking about.)
• Recurring tasks completely disappear from the app if they are not currently due, so you can’t look ahead to see what recurring tasks you have coming up - though you can find them individually by searching in Google Calendar. Why Google Calendar has a search function that works on Tasks, while Tasks doesn’t, is beyond me
• Tasks can only have one set of subtasks - which cannot be hidden
• Longer Task notes get visually truncated, so you can’t see past a certain point
• No tags or hierarchical sorting
• Can’t rearrange the order of your Lists in the app, you have to do it via the web app
• Un-deletable ‘default’ list - as such, I recommend not using it 
• Recently added feature of “Due Dates” don’t seem to provide any sort of visual feedback in the app, not sure if they do in GC, also Due Dates are not editable in calendar despite being…dates
• I’m sure there was more…

Again, this is a Google app. A handful of small meaningful changes would put this squarely top of the heap, like most Google apps. But here we are.

reviews.title: Native Keep Reminders to Tasks kills functionality
reviews.text:
Because Keep reminders are now Tasks and only fire through Google Calendar or Tasks, I have to remember to open the Calendar or Tasks app so it syncs over after every new reminder is created. Otherwise, notifications will never fire or update properly
It also fails to pull the most recent edits of the note once created as a task - so if I add a last minute item to the top of the list later, it'll never update Tasks - even if I change the reminder time after it fires
If I don't open this app for a while (since I really only use Keep, not Tasks) - newly created reminders just never fire notifications
Very bad google , very bad…
